defiscan.label: Stage 0
defiscan.verbatim: Stage 0. Pendle is a yield-trading protocol that enables users to manage and optimize their yield exposure. By tokenizing yield-bearing assets into standardized yield tokens (SY), Pendle allows these assets to be split into principal tokens (PT) and yield tokens (YT). This separation facilitates various strategies, including earning fixed yields, speculating on future yield changes, and providing liquidity to earn additional rewards. Pendle's Automated Market Maker (AMM) is specifically designed to handle the trading of these assets.

keyFindings.title: 18 Unverified Contracts Across Core Infrastructure
keyFindings.description: 45% of discovered contracts (18/40) have no verified source on their respective block explorers, preventing independent bytecode audit. This includes ProxyAdmin (upgrade authority), sPENDLE (~33M supply), YieldContractFactoryV6 implementation on Ethereum, cross-chain bridge/oracle contracts on Ethereum, and all Pendle deployments on Plasma and HyperEVM.

keyFindings.title: Optimism PT OFT Factory Controlled by EOA
keyFindings.description: The Optimism PT OFT Adapter Factory (0x45Dd4aEcc425b01bf98C567407aB4a4fF3C7d349) owner is 0x1FcCC097db89A86Bfc474A1028F93958295b1Fb7 (Core Deployer), confirmed as an EOA via eth_getCode. This single externally-owned account can reconfigure cross-chain PT bridging on Optimism without multisig protection — a critical single point of failure for spoke-chain PT liquidity.

keyFindings.title: Unverified ProxyAdmin Controls Core Upgradeable Proxies
keyFindings.description: ProxyAdmin (0xA28c08f165116587D4F3E708743B4dEe155c5E64) is unverified but on-chain owns the TransparentUpgradeableProxy admin slots for MarketFactoryV6, SYFactory, PYYtLpOracle, LimitRouter, and YieldContractFactoryV6. ProxyAdmin owner is the 3/5 governance multisig (0x8119EC16...), enabling immediate implementation swaps with no observable timelock delay.

keyFindings.title: sPENDLE Token Bytecode Unverified
keyFindings.description: sPENDLE (0x999999999991E178D52Cd95AFd4b00d066664144) holds ~33.2M tokens in circulation and is owned by the 3/5 governance multisig, but its source is not verified on Etherscan. Mint, burn, and staking mechanics cannot be independently audited despite sPENDLE being the active governance staking token (vePENDLE deprecated).

keyFindings.title: YieldContractFactoryV6 Implementation Unverified on Ethereum
keyFindings.description: YieldContractFactoryV6 proxy (0x3E6EBa46AbC5ab18ED95F6667d8B2fd4020E4637) delegates to implementation 0x21414e68da7658b5b2d9c04b06a1f03055763087 via ProxyAdmin, but neither the factory address nor its implementation is verified on Etherscan. This factory deploys yield contracts (PT/YT) that hold user funds.

keyFindings.title: Cross-Chain Bridge and Oracle Stack Unverified on Ethereum
keyFindings.description: Three Ethereum contracts in the cross-chain PT pipeline are unverified: SenderEndpoint (0x07b1014c...), PT OFT Adapter Factory (0x905aF80C...), and Cross-Chain Exchange Rate Oracle (0xA914c44E...). PT OFT Factory and CrossChainOracle are owned by the 2/5 Dev Multisig; SenderEndpoint by the 3/5 governance multisig. Bridge configuration (setPeer/setOracle equivalents) cannot be audited from source.

keyFindings.title: No Timelock on Proxy Upgrades
keyFindings.description: Core factories, oracles, and routers use OpenZeppelin TransparentUpgradeableProxy pattern with a central ProxyAdmin. On-chain verification shows upgrades can be executed immediately by the 3/5 governance multisig via ProxyAdmin.upgrade() — no timelock contract is interposed between governance and implementation changes.

keyFindings.title: No Timelock on Admin Actions or Upgrades
keyFindings.description: On-chain verification found no TimelockController or delay mechanism on ProxyAdmin, PendleGovernanceProxy (UUPS), or core factory proxies. The 3-of-5 governance multisig can execute upgrades, parameter changes, and batched admin calls via PendleGovernanceProxy.aggregate() immediately. PENDLE token config changes have a 7-day delay, but contract upgrades do not.

keyFindings.title: Cross-Chain Governance Threshold Asymmetry on Optimism
keyFindings.description: Per-chain Gnosis Safe governance proxies use different signer sets and thresholds. Optimism governance Safe (0xa06C863fcf17cA6f24AA81aeA75E23953193fF6A) is 2-of-4, while Ethereum (0x8119…ee1), Arbitrum/Base (0x7877…75Ac), and BSC (0xA066…a9Ec) are 3-of-5 with overlapping signer sets. Optimism is the weakest governance link for chain-specific actions.

keyFindings.title: Per-Asset SY Adapter Contagion
keyFindings.description: Pendle core wraps yield via permissionless Standardized Yield (SY) adapters that call external protocols (Curve, Balancer, Benqi/QiToken, etc.). ChainSecurity and Spearbit audits explicitly exclude derived SY implementations. A compromised or misconfigured SY adapter can poison exchangeRate(), affecting PT/YT pricing, cross-chain oracle feeds, and any integrator relying on Pendle markets.

keyFindings.title: Penpie Third-Party Exploit — Sep 2024 ($27M)
keyFindings.description: On Sep 3, 2024, Penpie (yield optimizer built on Pendle) lost ~$27M via reentrancy in batchHarvestMarketRewards. Attacker created malicious Pendle markets using permissionless market creation with fake SY contracts. Pendle contracts were not exploited; Pendle detected the attack, paused all contracts within ~1 hour, and reportedly prevented ~$70–105M in additional losses across dependent protocols. Contracts later unpaused. Penpie users were not compensated by Pendle.

keyFindings.title: Cross-Chain Governance Threshold Divergence
keyFindings.description: Governance multisig thresholds differ across chains: Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and BSC use 3/5, while Optimism uses 2/4. Weaker quorum on Optimism reduces the number of signers required for governance actions on that chain's deployments.
